title: POC Weekly Sync - Security & Compliance Review
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on security/compliance questions — SSO integration timing, audit log format and retention, SOC 2 evidence request, and a couple of tuning items from the performance run. Action items captured and next steps agreed: Redwood to share SOC 2 report and audit-log schema, customer to validate SSO test account and retention window, schedule follow-up baseline run after SSO is in place.
action_items: Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Share latest SOC 2 Type II and evidence binder link by 2025-02-14
Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE): Export audit-log schema and sample logs, include field mappings and retention config by 2025-02-14
Liam O'Connor (NovaPay): Provision SAML test account and send metadata to Redwood by 2025-02-16
Rao (NovaPay): Confirm data retention window and deletion requirements, reply by 2025-02-18
Kevin Liu (Redwood CSM): Schedule next POC baseline run for week of 2025-02-24 and invite stakeholders
next_steps: Redwood to provide SOC 2 report and security whitepaper link
Customer to validate SSO test account and confirm SAML metadata
Redwood SE to share audit log export and retention options
Agree on retention policy for pilot artifacts (logs, prompts, outputs)
Schedule follow-up POC run after SSO verification and compare token-level audit logs
transcript:
Header: 2025-02-12 10:00 PST | Duration: ~45 mins | Meeting ID: ff-20250212-0034
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Kevin Liu (Redwood CSM); Sara Patel (NovaPay Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (PM), Rao (Devops)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Morning everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick agenda — brief recap of last week's benchmark, then security items SSO/audit logs/retention, and then action items. Sara, quick opening?

[00:12] Sara Patel: Hey all, yes thanks. We want to make sure the pilot aligns with our compliance constraints. Main things today are SSO SAML, where audit logs live and how long they stay, and getting a copy of Redwood's SOC 2. Also we saw some logs from last run that didn't have request IDs so it's hard to match trace events.

[00:28] Daniel Ortiz: Got it. On the trace IDs — that was something we saw in the staging run; the KV cache prefixing added extra fields and our exporter didn't include the request_id consistently, we'll patch that. For SSO, Maya, do we have the SAML SP metadata and the config doc?

[00:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a SAML guide — I uploaded it to the shared drive earlier, link in the notes. We support SAML 2.0 with IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows, plus SCIM for provisioning if you want. For the POC we recommended IdP-initiated to start — less friction.

[00:58] Liam O'Connor: We'll likely do IdP-initiated first. Rao, can you spin up a test IdP user?

[01:04] Rao: Yep I can do that today. I'll need the metadata file from Redwood.

[01:08] Maya Chen: I'll send the metadata after the call. Note the EntityID is the redwood host name and the ACS URL needs to be whitelisted in your IdP.

[01:15] Priya Singh: On retention — NovaPay has a 90-day retention max for logs containing PII. We need to confirm what fields Redwood stores in audit logs and whether we're able to configure deletion after the pilot.

[01:25] Daniel Ortiz: Our audit logs capture request metadata, timestamps, model name, token counts, request_id, user_id if client sets one, and we can optionally include a redacted copy of the prompt or just a hash. By default hosted retains logs for 30 days, but for Dedicated/Private you control retention. For the pilot on hosted, we can set a custom retention policy though it requires agreement — and we can auto-delete prompt text after X days.

[01:47] Sara Patel: Important: we can't have raw prompts with PII beyond 30 days. Also need assurance the logs are immutable for the retention window for audit purposes. How do you handle write-once for logs?

[01:58] Daniel Ortiz: We push logs to an append-only store with object versioning and a write-ahead log. For hosted we provide read-only S3 export -- the retention and deletion job runs by scheduled lifecycle policy. For Dedicated we support forward-integration to your SIEM. I'll include the export schema and retention config in the doc.

[02:14] Sara Patel: Are those exports encrypted with customer-managed keys?

[02:18] Maya Chen: Yes — we support KMS-based encryption. For Private/Dedicated we can point to your KMS/HSM; for hosted we offer CMEK with a partner HSM. I'll note caveats in the SOC2 doc.

[02:29] Priya Singh: SOC 2 — we need the Type II report and any supporting evidence for the last 12 months. We requested it in the last email but haven't received it yet.

[02:37] Maya Chen: Apologies for the delay, the Type II bundle is ready. I'll share the secure link after the call — expect the binder and a summary PDF. For sensitive artifacts we can gate it behind an NDA portal if needed.

[02:48] Sara Patel: Good. We'll need the list of controls covered and the auditor name. Also any SOC 2 scope exclusions.

[02:55] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll include control mapping to your compliance checklist.

[03:02] Liam O'Connor: Back to SSO — what's the expected lead time to get SAML running end-to-end? Once we give you metadata, how long until we can validate?

[03:10] Daniel Ortiz: Typically IdP-initiated takes 1-3 business days in our experience: we exchange metadata, we configure the tenant, you test, we iterate. If you want SCIM provisioning that's another touch but can be done in 1 week.

[03:22] Rao: That's fine. We'll try to get the test user in place by Monday.

[03:27] Priya Singh: About audit logs — we want token-level accounting for billing reconciliation. Can Redwood provide a per-token token-breakdown with cost attribution per request?

[03:38] Kevin Liu: Yes, our Console provides token-level cost breakdowns per request and per model. For the POC we can enable detailed telemetry and export CSV with token_count, model, cost_estimate, and request_id. Note that the detailed export may include prompt excerpts if enabled — we can hash or redact those fields per your policy.

[03:55] Sara Patel: We will ask for hashed prompt values, not raw text. Also need to confirm the export delivery method — S3 push or API pull?

[04:03] Daniel Ortiz: Both supported. We can push to a customer-owned S3 with server-side encryption, or you can pull via our secure API. We'll include sample event payloads.

[04:12] Priya Singh: Any compliance gaps we should be aware of for the hosted pilot vs a Dedicated deployment?

[04:18] Maya Chen: Main differences: hosted is faster to start but has less tenant-level isolation; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, dedicated network, and full control of retention/keys. For certain regulated controls you may need Dedicated or Private — we'll map that into the control matrix. But for a short pilot with a 30-90 day retention window, hosted with CMEK and SAML is often acceptable.

[04:40] Sara Patel: For audit we need immutable logs and chain of custody. Can you sign attestation for the pilot that logs won't be modified during the retention window?

[04:48] Kevin Liu: We can provide a pilot-level attestation describing the logging pipeline and retention enforcement. It won't be a formal third-party attestation but it documents technical controls and lifecycle policies.

[04:59] Priya Singh: Fine, that helps for our internal auditors.

[05:03] Maya Chen: Quick note on the bench run: last week's baseline showed 12% token cost reduction when we enabled prefix caching, but latency tail increased slightly at 99th percentile because of batching behavior under burst. We recommended slightly lower max_batch_size to trade a bit of throughput for lower tail latency.

[05:21] Liam O'Connor: Can you give us the config that produced the 12% reduction? We want to replicate it in our environment but also ensure it doesn't surface new PII in logs.

[05:31] Daniel Ortiz: Will share the runtime config: cache enabled, max_batch_size 64, batching_window 20ms; and a note about masking prompt content in logs. We'll also include sample scripts to run the benchmark on your side.

[05:44] Sara Patel: Last question — retention for prompt/response artifacts during the pilot: can we set auto-delete of raw prompts after 7 days and keep hashed artifacts for 90 days?

[05:56] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, that's doable for hosted pilot — we'll set the lifecycle to delete raw prompt text after 7 days, keep hashed references and token accounting for 90 days. We'll include the lifecycle policy in the audit doc.

[06:08] Priya Singh: Great. Anything on legal/procurement?

[06:12] Maya Chen: Procurement asked us to note that if you opt into Dedicated later, contract language changes for SLA and data residency. For the POC we'll stick to the standard trial T&Cs — Kevin will follow up with procurement points.

[06:22] Kevin Liu: I'll send a short procurement checklist after the call and loop in our legal team.

[06:28] Sara Patel: OK let's recap next steps.

[06:31] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood shares SOC2 and evidence binder, Redwood SE shares audit-log schema and sample payloads, customer provisions SAML test account, customer confirms retention windows and PII policy, and Redwood to schedule baseline rerun after SSO is validated. Any additions?

[06:46] Priya Singh: Please include the sample event schema with field-level descriptions and redaction knobs.

[06:52] Daniel Ortiz: Will do.

[06:55] Rao: I'll aim to have the test account and metadata out by Monday.

[06:59] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with those artifacts. Thanks everyone, we'll send meeting notes and action items.

[07:06] Sara Patel: Thanks all.

[07:09] End of recording

Notes: Link to SOC2 and security docs to be provided by Redwood post-call; audit-log schema and sample payloads promised; benchmark tuning knobs shared as runtime config. Some transcription noise present in timestamps and minor name spellings (e.g., Rao sometimes labeled as "Raw").
